sentences.text: ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

The present appeal is filed by the appellant-Union of India under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, being NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4898/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/09/2024 undefined aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 30.4.2007 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Ahmedabad (Rural) in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.1986 of 1991, by which, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding the compensation of Rs.2,78,360/- with interest @ 7.5% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization,, to be recovered from the opponent.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Petition No.1986 of 1991
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
2. The facts of the present appeals are as under :
2.1 The claimant/s filed the claim petition stating that on 16.11.1991, at about 11.45 p.m., near Ambali road station, opposite Thaltej gam, at railway crossing gate no.11,
the accident took place; that the decease plying auto rickshaw bearing no.GRT 163 and that the deceased was driving rickshaw in slow speed and while crossing the railway crossing gate, one goods train came suddenly and dashed with the rickshaw due to which the accident occurred and the deceased died.
Therefore, the claimants filed the claim petition claiming compensation.
2.2 The notice was served to the opponent.
The opponent filed the written statement denying the contents of the claim petition.
The issues were framed by the Tribunal.
Oral as well as documentary evidence were led before the Tribunal.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4898/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/09/2024 undefined
After hearing the submissions made by the rival parties, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition(s) and awarded compensation as noted above.
2.3 Hence, the opponent-Union of India has filed the present appeal before this Court.

3. Learned advocate for the appellant has mainly submitted that the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal has no jurisdiction to try the claim petition as the goods train is not a motor vehicle under the Motor Vehicles Act; that the claimants have not examined any independent witness; that the gate was closed and the rickshaw driver dashed with bamboo and he fell out of the rickshaw and there was no scope for the rickshaw to enter the gate and therefore the railway authorities are not liable to make the payment.

She further contended that the insurance company of the auto rickshaw is not joined as party to the proceedings and therefore the judgment relied on by the learned Tribunal in the case of Union of India V/s Bhagwati Prasad will not be helpful to the claimants.

entities.text: Union of India V/s Bhagwati Prasad
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
She,
therefore, submitted that the appeal be allowed.
4. There is no representation on behalf of the claimants.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4898/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/09/2024 undefined Union Of India vs Indiraben Wd/O.

5. I have considered the submissions made at the bar.
I have perused the record and proceedings.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
I have also considered the pleadings of the parties before the Tribunal.

5.1 As far as the negligence aspect is concerned, the complaint filed by the complainant PSI states that the rickshaw dashed with bamboo of gate no.11 and dashed with the goods train and caused the accident; the panchanama shows that the gate no.11 was opened and so the rickshaw dashed with the goods train; however, there is no mention in the complaint or the panchanama that the bamboo was anyway affected or was found broken and the rickshaw would not have reached to dash with the goods train without causing substantial damage to the bamboo, if at all it dashed with the bamboo.

This shows that the railway crossing is a manned crossing and it is to be adversely inferred that the gate was not closed due to some delay on behalf of the railway gate man due to which, not knowing that the goods train is coming, the rickshaw driver-deceased tried to cross the crossing and dashed with the goods train.

Further, it transpires from the record that neither the driver of the train who was on duty at the relevant time was examined nor the gateman of Crossman who was on duty was NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4898/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/09/2024 undefined examined by the appellant-opponent to rebut the say of the claimants as well as the documentary evidence.
Therefore, there cannot be any second view to be taken holding contributory negligence on the part of the deceased and the railway authorities are solely negligent and liable to pay the compensation.

5.2 When the negligence aspect is proved, the judgment of Bhagwati Prasad (supra), will be applicable to the facts of the case, wherein it is stated as under:
"

xxxxx Having said so it was further held that if it is ultimately found that there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the vehicle or there is no defect in the vehicle but the accident is only due to the sole negligence of other parties/agencies then on that finding the claim would go out of sec.110 of the Act because the case would become exclusive negligence of Railways and again if the accident had arisen only on account of the negligence of persons other than the driver/owner of the motor vehicle the claim would not be maintainable before the Tribunal.

......In other words, in such a case also the Motor Vehicle Claims Tribunal would be entitled to award compensation against the other joint tortfeasor, and in the case in hand, it would be fully justified to award compensation against the Railway Administration if ultimately it is held that it was the sole NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4898/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/09/2024 undefined negligence on the part of the Railway Administration."

5.3 Therefore, in view of the above, the learned Tribunal had jurisdiction to try the claim petition and the learned Tribunal has passed the impugned judgment and award relying the judgment of the Bhagwati Prasad (supra) itself.

Further, as stated in the judgment of Bhagwati Prasad (supra), in absence of the insurance company of the auto rickshaw being joined in the claim petition also, when the railways are solely negligent for the accident in question, the learned Tribunal has not committed any error in holding the appellant liable to pay the compensation.
If the deceased would have been negligent for the accident, the case would have been different.

Therefore, the appeal is not Union Of India vs Indiraben Wd/O. Panchpadhi Thandapani on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46402931/
3 required to be entertained on this count.

5.3 A reference to the judgment in the case of Union of India V/s United India Insurance Co.Ltd.
And Others, it is observed and held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in head-note as under:
"Under Section 13 of the Railways Act, 1890 no such duties are imposed directly on the Railway administration by the statute.

entities.text:
Union of India V/s United India Insurance Co.Ltd.
And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The section on the other hand only confers a power on the Central Government to issue a requisition to the Railway administration, i.e. the General Managers or the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4898/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/09/2024 undefined Railway Companies (if any) to take steps as per Section 13.

Obviously, if the Central Government does not think fit to exercise that power and does not issue any such requisition, the occasion for the Railway administration to take steps under Section 13, as per the statutory mandate, will not arise.
Thus, the statutory duties of the Railway administration under Section 13, do not arise unless a requisition is made by the Central Government.
The above anomaly has naturally compelled the courts to fall back upon the common law duties resting on the Railways.

The law in this behalf is again well settled that the claimants can at their choice sue the Railways to enforce either or both types of these duties, i.e., under common law as well as under the statute.
The claimants can sue the Railways concurrently for breach of the common law or statutory duties or for breach of either of the duties.
As regard the nature of duty of the Railways at level- crossings from time to time?
In the same decision of the Privy Council in Commr. for Rlys. v. McDermott.

It has been stated that the Railways' duty of care at common law is based on the principle of neighbourhood laid down by Lord Atkin in Donoghue v. Stevenson by Lord Atkin who said "You must take reasonable care to avoid acts or omission which you can reasonably foresee would be likely to injure your neighbour."

The duty to care at common law NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4898/2008 JUDGMENT DATED:
12/09/2024 undefined is therefore based upon the dangerous or perilous nature of the operations of the Railways.

The test of breach of common law duty is again the test of a reasonable or prudent person in the particular fact situation -- of course the amount of care, skill, diligence or the like, varying according to the circumstances of the particular case.
The standard of foresight is again that of a reasonable person.
Such a person is also expected to take into account common negligence in human behaviour.

Of course, he need not anticipate folly in all its forms because the Railways are involved in what is recognised as dangerous or perilous operations, they are at common law, to take reasonable and necessary care, on the "neighbourhood" principle -- even if the provisions in Section 13(c) and (d) of the Railways Act, 1890 are not attracted for want of requisition by the Central Government.

sentences.text: 4 It is the common law duty on the part of the Railway if it does not take notice of the increase in the volume of rail and motor traffic at the unmanned level-crossing and if it does not take adequate steps such as putting up gates with a watchman so as to prevent accidents at such a point.
In the case before us the Railways have led no independent evidence of any application of mind to these issues.

Obviously, the Railways presumed that the negligence of the driver of the bus could be imputed to the passengers but NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4898/2008 JUDGMENT DATED:
12/09/2024 undefined this, as stated by us under Point 2 is legally untenable.

The High Court has noticed that 300 vehicles pass through this point and six express trains cut across this public road every day (obviously there must be other non-express or passenger trains and goods trains every day).
The population was also dense near about the place.

In Lloyds case [(1952) 1 All ER 1248, CA] the Court of Appeal thought that even when the road traffic reached a level of 75 to 100 vehicles,
the Railways ought to have, if it was a public road, put gates and a watchman, as required by statute.

The High Court, in our view, rightly observed that the bus driver was from Tamil Nadu, he was not familiar with this place in Kerala State where the accident occurred, there was no caution board or other indication to show that the road was cutting across a railway line, and there were no gates or handrails to alert the passers-by.
It was held that if the Railways had taken adequate precautionary measures such as, erecting hand rails or gates, a severe accident like this would not have taken place.
In the absence of gates and caution board, the level-crossing was held to be in the nature of a trap.

Therefore, applying common law principles, the Railways must also be deemed to be negligent in not converting the unmanned level-crossing into a manned one with gates -- having regard to the volume of rail and road traffic at this point"

In view of the above judgment also, there is no NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4898/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/09/2024 undefined error committed by the learned Tribunal in passing the impugned judgment and award.
8. In view of above, the following order is passed.
8.1 The present appeal is dismissed with no order as to costs.

8.2 The amount lying with the Tribunal and/or in the FDR, pursuant to the order of this Court if any, shall be disbursed to the claimant, along with accrued interest thereon if any, by account payee cheque, after proper verification and after following due procedure, within a period of six weeks from today.
8.3 Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.

(SANDEEP N. BHATT,J) SRILATHA Union Of India vs Indiraben Wd/O. Panchpadhi Thandapani on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46402931/
